import os

import pytest

# Import the public API that is available in the project
from doorstop.core import builder, find_item, find_document, Tree
from doorstop.core.document import Document
from doorstop.core.item import Item


# Helper to create a simple requirement file
def _create_req_file(path, uid, title="Test requirement", content=""):
    """Create a YAML requirement file with the given UID."""
    yaml = textwrap.dedent(
        f"""
        id: {uid}
        title: {title}
        content: {content}
        """
    )
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(yaml.strip() + "\n")


@pytest.fixture
def temp_dir(tmp_path):
    """Return a temporary directory that is cleaned up after the test."""
    return tmp_path


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Test case: U02_4__xUnit_Test_C__TC_001  (Test requirement storage)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_U02_4__xUnit_Test_C__TC_001(temp_dir):
    """
    Test requirement storage
    Expected: Requirement is stored successfully
    """
    # Arrange: create a requirement file
    req_path = temp_dir / "REQ001.yml"
    _create_req_file(req_path, "REQ001", "Initial requirement")

    # Act: build the tree from the temp directory
    tree = builder.build(cwd=str(temp_dir))

    # Assert: the requirement is present in the tree
    item = tree.find_item("REQ001")
    assert item is not None, "Requirement REQ001 should be found in the tree"
    assert isinstance(item, Item), "Found object should be an Item instance"
    assert item.uid == "REQ001", "Item UID should match the requirement ID"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Test case: U02_4__xUnit_Test_C__TC_002  (Test requirement change management)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_U02_4__xUnit_Test_C__TC_002(temp_dir):
    """
    Test requirement change management
    Expected: Requirement is updated successfully
    """
    # Arrange: create initial requirement
    req_path = temp_dir / "REQ001.yml"
    _create_req_file(req_path, "REQ001", "Initial requirement")

    # Build initial tree
    tree = builder.build(cwd=str(temp_dir))
    item = tree.find_item("REQ001")
    assert item is not None

    # Act: modify the requirement file
    _create_req_file(req_path, "REQ001", "Updated requirement")

    # Rebuild the tree to reflect changes
    tree_updated = builder.build(cwd=str(temp_dir))
    item_updated = tree_updated.find_item("REQ001")
    assert item_updated is not None

    # Assert: the content has changed
    assert (
        item_updated.content != item.content
    ), "Requirement content should be updated after file modification"
    assert (
        "Updated requirement" in item_updated.content
    ), "Updated content should be present in the item"

def test_U02_4__xUnit_Test_C__TC_004(temp_dir):
    """
    Test requirement scalability
    Expected: Requirement is retrieved successfully
    """
    # Arrange: create a large number of requirement files
    num_reqs = 1000
    for i in range(num_reqs):
        uid = f"REQ{i:04d}"
        _create_req_file(temp_dir / f"{uid}.yml", uid, f"Requirement {i}")

    # Act: build the tree
    tree = builder.build(cwd=str(temp_dir))

    # Assert: all requirements are present
    for i in range(num_reqs):
        uid = f"REQ{i:04d}"
        item = tree.find_item(uid)
        assert item is not None, f"Requirement {uid} should be found in the tree"
        assert item.uid == uid, f"Item UID should match {uid}"
